fr_passeport_noun.hook: A girl in a yellow raincoat shows her PASSPORT at the window while the rain POURS down: PASS, POUR! pahs-POR.
fr_passeport_noun.why: Duck in a raincoat replaced by a human girl (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_rendez_vous_noun.hook: A boy with a bouquet checks his pocket watch: his RENDEZVOUS is late! English borrowed the same word: rahn-day-VOO.
fr_rendez_vous_noun.why: Hedgehog replaced by a human boy (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_ficelle_noun.hook: TWINE is wound round the neck of a CELLO: fee-SEHL = fi-CELL(o)!
fr_ficelle_noun.why: Old hook described a shop-mouse that is not painted; the painted cello with twine is now the hook.

fr_stylo_noun.hook: A STYLISH PEN in a pink scarf leans on the desk, striking a pose: STY-LO! stee-LOH.
fr_stylo_noun.why: Desk zoom re-cut from the town hall painting; the pen there wears a pink scarf (its sunglasses are too small to see), so the hook names only what is visible.

fr_feuille_noun_2.hook: This SHEET of writing paper is cut in the shape of a LEAF, because French uses one word for both: une feuille (de papier).
fr_feuille_noun_2.why: RECS 1.4: paper sense split from the leaf (fr_feuille_noun, foret/arbres).

fr_ainsi_adv.hook: ANN ("an-") says "SEE ("-SEE")? You fold the ballot THUS, in this way" and shows the young man how to mail it in the box.
fr_ainsi_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_assez_adv.hook: A councillor keeps pouring water until the glass overflows, and the bald man beside her raises a hand: "I SAY ("ah-SAY"), that's ENOUGH!"
fr_assez_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_certainement_adv.hook: Like English 'certainly', said sehr-teh-nuh-MAHN: a knight councillor holds up all TEN fingers: "CERTAINLY, SIR, TEN times over!"
fr_certainement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_donc_adv.hook: The councillor brings down his gavel: DONK ("DOHNK")! SO, THEREFORE, the motion is passed.
fr_donc_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_enfin_adv.hook: After a sweltering wait, a councillor pulls the cord and the ceiling fan is finally ON: "ON FAN ("ahn-FAN"), AT LAST!"
fr_enfin_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_ensuite_adv.hook: The bearded councillor waits to speak NEXT, holding one big SWEET ("ahn-SWEET"): first the gavel, THEN it's his turn.
fr_ensuite_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_peut_etre_adv.hook: A gray-haired councillor's hand PUPPET ("peuh-TEHTR") shrugs its little shoulders: PERHAPS yes, PERHAPS no.
fr_peut_etre_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_seulement_adv.hook: A councillor proudly holds up a SALMON ("suh-luh-MAHN"): he caught ONLY one!
fr_seulement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_evidemment_adv.hook: Like English 'evidently', said ay-vee-dah-MAHN: A VIDEO MAN films the cat beside the pie, crumbs scattered round it: OF COURSE the cat nibbled the pie.
fr_evidemment_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_absolument_adv.hook: Like English 'absolutely', said ahp-soh-lew-MAHN: a red-haired councillor bangs the gallery rail and roars "ABSOLUTELY!", making every inkpot jump into the air.
fr_absolument_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_certes_adv.hook: "ADMITTEDLY, it's a CERT ("SEHRT")", smiles the gray-haired councillor, holding up her certificate with its red seal, "but let's vote anyway."
fr_certes_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_d_ailleurs_adv.hook: BESIDES the roses, the vase holds one big pink DAHLIA ("dah-YUHR").
fr_d_ailleurs_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_heureusement_adv.hook: FORTUNATELY the striped circus strongman dives and catches the falling pitcher just in time: "HURRAH'S ("uh-RUHZ") the MAN ("mon")!"
fr_heureusement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_probablement_adv.hook: Like English 'probably', said proh-bah-bluh-MAHN: a councillor at the gallery window grabs her umbrella as black clouds gather: it will PROBABLY rain.
fr_probablement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_completement_adv.hook: Like English 'completely', said kohn-pleh-tuh-MAHN: halfway through the debate an old councillor in a big white wig has fallen COMPLETELY asleep, eyes shut, chin on his hand.
fr_completement_adv.why: Painted v2 council chamber shows this scene; hook rewritten to match the painting.

fr_allemand_adj.hook: "Al, man!" ("ah-luh-MAHN") cries a pen pal from Berlin, waving a little GERMAN flag in the archives.
fr_allemand_adj.why: Painted live in the archives, not in an old photo.

fr_europeen_adj.hook: Like English 'European', said euh-roh-pay-AN: a girl files picture postcards from EUROPEAN places, a windmill and a leaning tower, into a long wooden drawer.
fr_europeen_adj.why: Stork replaced by a girl (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_francais_adj.hook: "France, eh?" ("frahn-SEH") says a visitor, opening a big FRENCH book tied with a blue-white-red ribbon.
fr_francais_adj.why: No text allowed, so the dictionary is a ribbon-tied book in French colors.

fr_local_adj.hook: Like English 'local', said loh-KAHL: the LOCAL baker gives a LOW CALL of "fresh bread!" through the archive window, holding up a basket of baguettes.
fr_local_adj.why: No line painted; the baker at the window carries the hook.

fr_etranger_adj.hook: A FOREIGN traveler with a sticker-covered suitcase walks into the archives: "Jay?" ("ay-trahn-ZHAY")
fr_etranger_adj.why: Painted arriving in the archives, not stepping off a train.

fr_belge_adj.hook: A BELGIAN waffle with a little black-yellow-red flag stuck on top.

fr_espagnol_adj.hook: A SPANISH spaniel ("ehs-pah-NYOL") dances flamenco on its hind legs, little bells ringing in its paws.
fr_espagnol_adj.why: The painted spaniel holds hand bells, not castanets.

fr_italien_adj.hook: Like English 'Italian', said ee-tah-LYAN: a gondolier named Ali, in a straw boater, sings an opera tune with an ITALIAN map rolled under his arm.
fr_italien_adj.why: Painted singing with the rolled map rather than filing it.

fr_parisien_adj.hook: Like English 'Parisian', said pah-ree-ZYAN: IAN in a navy coat holds up a PARISIAN postcard of the Eiffel Tower.
fr_parisien_adj.why: Striped sweater and beret removed (those belong to Monsieur Verbe).

fr_international_adj.hook: Like English 'international', said an-tehr-nah-syoh-NAHL: an archivist pins INTERNATIONAL picture postcards onto a big globe.
fr_international_adj.why: Stamps are too small to show; the postcards on the globe carry the hook.

fr_general_adj.hook: Like English 'general', said zhay-nay-RAHL: a GENERAL in medals sorts color-coded folders into one GENERAL drawer.
fr_general_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_mondial_adj.hook: A boy turns the "Mon" dial ("mohn-DYAHL") on a giant globe's stand to spin it WORLDWIDE.
fr_mondial_adj.why: The dial is painted on the stand with a boy turning it.

fr_national_adj.hook: Like English 'national', said nah-syoh-NAHL: an archivist folds a NATIONAL flag neatly into a box.
fr_national_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_particulier_adj.hook: Like English 'particular', said pahr-tee-kew-LYAY: a PARTY guest in a pointy hat is so PARTICULAR he lines up the archive shoe boxes by shoe size: "COOL, YAY!"
fr_particulier_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_politique_adj.hook: Like English 'political', said poh-lee-TEEK: POLLY the parrot squawks a POLITICAL speech from a carved TEAK podium.
fr_politique_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_africain_adj.hook: Like English 'African', said ah-free-KAN: an archivist holds up an AFRICAN map of the winding Nile, and a carved wooden giraffe stands close by.
fr_africain_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_americain_adj.hook: Like English 'American', said ah-may-ree-KAN: MARY files an AMERICAN map of the prairies and a postcard of a bison.
fr_americain_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_chinois_adj.hook: A CHINESE lantern glows over a little dragon as she ("shee-NWAH") waves a paper fan.
fr_chinois_adj.why: A dragon puppet stands in for the dragon parade.
fr_chinois_adj.note: 'C'est du chinois !' = it's all Greek to me. Never use it as a label for any Asian person.

fr_divers_adj.hook: Like English 'diverse', said dee-VEHR: VARIOUS objects spill out of an archive drawer: a compass, a feather, a key and a pair of DIVERS' flippers.
fr_divers_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_officiel_adj.hook: Like English 'official', said oh-fee-SYEHL: an OFFICIAL in a sash bangs a giant rubber stamp onto an archive paper.
fr_officiel_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_populaire_adj.hook: Like English 'popular', said poh-pew-LEHR: a fox family's LAIR under the map table is so POPULAR that children crowd round to peek in.
fr_populaire_adj.why: Real foxes (not anthropomorphic) and peeking children instead of autograph fans.

fr_royal_adj.hook: Like English 'royal', said rwah-YAHL: a ROYAL corgi in a tiny crown sits on a red velvet cushion.
fr_royal_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_social_adj.hook: Like English 'social', said soh-SYAHL: Uncle AL, very SOCIAL, chats cheerfully with everyone in line.
fr_social_adj.why: Hook rewritten to match the painted scene.

fr_liberte_noun.hook: Like English 'liberty', said lee-behr-TAY: a lady dressed as the Statue of LIBERTY raises her golden torch.

fr_societe_noun.hook: Like English 'society', said soh-syay-TAY: the ladies of the flower-hat SOCIETY pose proudly for their club portrait.
fr_societe_noun.why: Club ladies in flowered hats painted.

fr_population_noun.hook: Like English 'population', said poh-pew-lah-SYOHN: balloons POP as a lady clicks her counter to count the town's POPULATION.

fr_association_noun.hook: A SOCK for every member: a lady hands out matching striped socks to her club, the 'ah-SOCK-see-ah-syohn' (ASSOCIATION).

fr_union_noun.hook: Sounds like ONION ('ew-NYOHN'): a lady holds a giant onion tied with a ribbon, the sign of the UNION.
fr_union_noun.why: Giant onion with a ribbon painted.

fr_independance_noun.hook: IN-DEPENDANCE = dancing on her own: a girl twirls a ribbon and dances all by herself, full of INDEPENDENCE.

fr_communaute_noun.hook: Like English 'community', said koh-mew-noh-TAY: neighbors water a shared COMMUNITY vegetable planter together.

fr_egal_adj.hook: Two GALs ('ay-GAHL') sit perfectly level on a seesaw: EQUAL weight, EQUAL height.

fr_communiste_noun.hook: Like English 'communist', said koh-mew-NEEST: a man in a worker's flat cap waves a plain red flag toward a painted sunrise.
fr_communiste_noun.why: Red flag, flat cap; no symbols or text.

fr_droit_noun.hook: 'DRAW-ah!' ('drwah'): a man raises his RIGHT hand high with a giant pencil, ready to DRAW, claiming his RIGHT.
fr_droit_noun.why: Raised right hand with giant pencil.

fr_membre_noun.hook: Like English 'member', said MAHM-bruh: a proud MEMBER shows off his blank membership card and rosette.
fr_membre_noun.why: Blank card with rosette; no text.
fr_membre_noun.note: In anatomy it can also mean the male organ; the context makes it clear.

fr_refuge_noun.hook: Like English 'refuge', said ruh-FEWZH: a man holds an umbrella over a leaky little shelter so the kittens have a REFUGE from the rain.

fr_clan_noun.hook: Like English 'clan', said KLAHN: three men in matching red plaid kilts, one family CLAN.

fr_esclavage_noun.hook: L'ESCLAVAGE ('ess-klah-VAHZH', slavery): a sensitive word, so it is not drawn. It sits on a plain blank museum plaque on a roped-off marble pedestal; the word itself is the hook.
fr_esclavage_noun.why: Mature/sensitive word: museum-style blank plaque, word shown only as the HTML label; velvet rope = neutral 'exhibit' cue.
fr_esclavage_noun.note: A heavy historical subject (France abolished slavery in 1848), so use it with care.

fr_manifestation_noun.hook: LA MANIFESTATION ('mah-nee-fess-tah-SYOHN'): MANY FEST! Many festive marchers parade with blank placards on sticks and a big drum.
fr_manifestation_noun.why: Sound-alike MANY + FEST: a cheerful crowd marching with placards = a demonstration.

fr_pauvrete_noun.hook: LA PAUVRETÉ ('poh-vruh-TAY', poverty): a sensitive word, so it is not drawn. It sits on a plain blank framed plaque on a low wooden stand; the word itself is the hook.
fr_pauvrete_noun.why: Grave/sensitive word: museum-style blank plaque, word shown only as the HTML label.

fr_commune_noun.hook: LA COMMUNE ('koh-MUEN'): COMMON! A man proudly holds a model of his little village built around its green COMMON, with one toy cow grazing.
fr_commune_noun.why: Sound-alike COMMON: a village round its common = the commune (smallest French local district).

fr_solidarite_noun.hook: LA SOLIDARITÉ ('soh-lee-dah-ree-TAY'): SOLID! Four friends link arms and stand together on one big SOLID granite block.
fr_solidarite_noun.why: Sound-alike SOLID: standing together, arms linked, on solid rock = solidarity.

fr_tribu_noun.hook: LA TRIBU ('tree-BUE'): TREE-BOO! A whole three-generation family, grandparents to kids, pops out from behind a potted TREE shouting BOO!
fr_tribu_noun.why: Sound-alike TREE + BOO; a big extended family group = a tribe (no costume shorthand).

fr_foire_noun.hook: LA FOIRE ('FWAHR'): FOUR! A girl carries a toy fair merry-go-round with exactly FOUR little horses.
fr_foire_noun.why: Sound-alike FOUR; the merry-go-round = a fair. Count: 4 horses.

fr_generosite_noun.hook: LA GÉNÉROSITÉ ('zhay-nay-roh-zee-TAY'): GENEROUS CITY! A boy hands his whole big fruit pie to another boy to share.
fr_generosite_noun.why: Sound-alike GENEROUS + CITY: giving away the whole pie = generosity.

fr_egalite_noun.hook: L'ÉGALITÉ ('ay-gah-lee-TAY'): EGG-ALITY! A brass scale hangs perfectly LEVEL with one identical white EGG in each pan.
fr_egalite_noun.why: Sound-alike EGG; equal eggs, level scale = equality. Its twin l'inégalité is the tipped scale next to it.

fr_inegalite_noun.hook: L'INÉGALITÉ ('ee-nay-gah-lee-TAY'): IN-EGG-ALITY! The second scale is steeply TIPPED: one huge EGG sinks low, one tiny egg flies high.
fr_inegalite_noun.why: Sound-alike EGG; near-synonym cue: tipped scale with unequal eggs vs the level scale of l'égalité.

fr_participation_noun.hook: LA PARTICIPATION ('par-tee-see-pah-SYOHN'): PARTY! A boy in a pointed PARTY hat shoots his hand up, eager to join in.
fr_participation_noun.why: Sound-alike PARTY: hand up to take part = participation.

fr_surement_adv.hook: Said sew-ruh-MAHN: a SURE-footed mountain goat SURELY strolls along the top of the council benches.
fr_surement_adv.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: removed 'Like English X' (not a cognate).

fr_vraiment_adv.hook: A donkey BRAYS at a MAN ("vreh-MAHN") with raised eyebrows: "REALLY? REALLY?!"
fr_vraiment_adv.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (vray-MON) -> (vreh-MAHN) to match the card.

fr_cependant_adv.hook: "HOWEVER hungry you are, DAN, the SAUCEPAN ("suh-pahn-DAHN") is empty!", HOWEVER, there is a cookie.
fr_cependant_adv.why: Text pass 2026-10-28 (hook lint): respelling (suh-pon-DON) -> (suh-pahn-DAHN) to match the card.

fr_poubelle_noun.hook: The big green TRASH CAN has a BELL on its lid that rings every time you throw something in: pou-BELLE! (It is named after Monsieur Poubelle, who brought trash cans to Paris.)
fr_poubelle_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_file_noun.hook: Three EELS wait patiently in a LINE at the town hall, the first one holding its ticket. Eel... FEEL! La file is the line.
fr_file_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_colis_noun.hook: A fluffy COLLIE dog proudly carries the PACKAGE in its mouth: koh-LEE = collie.
fr_colis_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_mairie_noun.hook: "may-REE": a bride and groom who have just come to MARRY at the TOWN HALL cut their wedding cake: MARRY
fr_mairie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a smiling bride in a white dress and a groom in a gray suit cutting a three-tier white wedding cake together, rose petals scattered on the floor.
fr_mairie_noun.note: La mairie is the town hall of a commune; in France every civil wedding takes place there, in front of the mayor.

fr_accorder_verb.hook: "ah-kor-DAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret), an ACCORDION strapped to his chest, GRANTS the newlyweds the big gold key of the town, tied with a red bow: A-CORD-AY: ACCORDION
fr_accorder_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing on a low wooden step with a red accordion strapped on his chest, holding out a big gold key with a red bow toward the wedding couple, his other hand raised in a flourish.
fr_accorder_verb.note: Accorder means to grant or to give (accorder une faveur, accorder dix minutes); it also means to tune an instrument (accorder un piano). S'accorder: to agree, or to go well together (des couleurs qui s'accordent).

fr_ministre_noun.hook: "mee-NEESTR": a stately MINISTER in a dark suit sips punch through a teeny MINI STRAW from a tall punch glass: MINI-STRAW
fr_ministre_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a tall gray-haired woman minister in a dark navy suit sipping pink punch from a tall glass through a tiny mini drinking straw.
fr_ministre_noun.note: Un ministre heads a government department; the word is masculine or feminine (le/la ministre). Not a church minister: that is un pasteur.

fr_president_noun.hook: "pray-zee-DAHN": everyone PRAISES DON, the club PRESIDENT, who blushes and lifts a gold trophy cup over his head: PRAISE-E-DON
fr_president_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a round-faced man with a gray mustache and a gold chain of office around his neck lifting a big gold trophy cup over his head, blushing, two guests beside him clapping.
fr_president_noun.note: Président also means the chair of a club, a meeting or a company (le président du club).

fr_depute_noun.hook: "day-pew-TAY": a DEPUTY in a suit with a tricolor sash taps a golf PUTT across the parquet toward a little golf hole on a green felt mat: DAY-PUTT-AY
fr_depute_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a young man with a short beard in a dark suit and a blue-white-red sash across his chest, crouched over a golf putter, tapping a white golf ball across the parquet floor toward a little golf cup hole in a small green felt putting mat.
fr_depute_noun.note: Un député is an elected member of the Assemblée nationale (a member of Parliament, like a U.S. representative), not a sheriff's deputy.

fr_ministere_noun.hook: "mee-nees-TEHR": on a round table stands a big model of the MINISTRY, and a little boy walks two fingers up its MINI STAIRcase: MINI-STAIR
fr_ministere_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a big white scale model of a grand columned government building with a wide sweeping mini staircase, on a round table, a little boy walking two fingers up the tiny stairs.
fr_ministere_noun.note: Un ministère is a government department and its building (le ministère de la Culture).

fr_congres_noun.hook: "kohn-GREH": a waiter brings a tray of GRAY ice-cream CONES to the CONGRESS delegates, who stare at the strange gray scoops: CONE-GRAY
fr_congres_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/honneur (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a waiter in a white jacket holding up a silver tray of five ice-cream cones with gray scoops, two delegates in suits with lanyards peering at them in surprise.
fr_congres_noun.note: Un congrès is a large formal meeting or conference (un congrès de médecins); in the U.S., le Congrès is Congress.

fr_signature_noun.hook: "see-nyah-TEWR": a TOUR guide holding up a little yellow pennant signs her name with a big swirly SIGNATURE while her tourists in sun hats wave 'SEE YA!': SEE-YA-TOUR
fr_signature_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a woman tour guide holding up a small yellow pennant on a stick in one hand and signing a large sheet of paper on a standing desk with the other, two tourists in sun hats and cameras on straps waving goodbye.
fr_signature_noun.note: La signature is both your signature and the act of signing (la signature du contrat).

fr_demarche_noun.hook: "day-MAHRSH": a man with an armful of forms MARCHES like a drum major from counter to counter, knees high: the long DÉMARCHE (process): DAY-MARCH
fr_demarche_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a man in a brown cardigan marching with high knees like a drum major, a big armful of papers held to his chest, crossing the floor between two counters.
fr_demarche_noun.note: Also means a person's walk or gait (une démarche élégante) and a step taken to get something done (faire des démarches).

fr_dossier_noun.hook: "doh-SYAY": a young DOE pokes her head over the counter and nibbles the corner of a fat DOSSIER (file) a clerk holds out: DOE-SEE-AY
fr_dossier_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a young spotted deer doe poking her head over the wooden counter and nibbling the corner of a thick tan cardboard file folder that a surprised clerk with glasses is holding.
fr_dossier_noun.note: Second sense: the back of a chair (le dossier de la chaise).

fr_sceau_noun.hook: "SOH": a gray-haired lady SEWS a red ribbon onto the document while the clerk beside her presses a brass SEAL into a blob of red wax on it: SEW
fr_sceau_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a gray-haired lady with glasses in a lilac cardigan sewing a ribbon onto a large paper with a needle and thread, and beside her a young clerk in a blue cardigan pressing a brass seal stamp into a blob of red wax with a red ribbon on the same paper.
fr_sceau_noun.note: Same sound as seau (bucket), saut (jump) and sot (fool): only the spelling sceau means seal.

fr_document_noun.hook: "doh-kew-MAHN": a DOCtor in a white coat points with a billiard CUE at the notice board where the important DOCUMENTs go: DOC-CUE-MAN
fr_document_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a doctor in a white coat with a stethoscope pointing with a long wooden billiard cue at a big cork notice board.
fr_document_noun.note: Like English document; also a computer file (un document Word).

fr_permis_noun.hook: "pehr-MEE": a freckled teenage boy with a fresh curly red PERM, still in pink rollers, proudly holds up his new driver's PERMIT: PERM-ME
fr_permis_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/papiers (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a grinning freckled red-haired teenage boy in a green sweater, his fresh curly perm still in pink rollers, holding up a small pink card.
fr_permis_noun.note: Le permis de conduire is a driver's license; un permis de construire is a building permit.

fr_pancarte_noun.hook: "pahn-KAHRT": a cook pushes a CART full of shiny frying PANS, and a big blank PLACARD on a pole sticks up out of it: PAN-CART
fr_pancarte_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a cheerful cook in a white apron pushing a wooden hand cart piled with shiny copper frying pans, a big blank white placard on a tall wooden pole standing up out of the cart.
fr_pancarte_noun.note: Une pancarte is any sign or placard: a notice on a door or a sign carried in a march.

fr_banderole_noun.hook: "bahn-duh-ROL": a little marching BAND plays under the long blank BANNER they have just unROLLed across the hall: BAND-A-ROLL
fr_banderole_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): two band musicians in red jackets and bowler hats, a trumpeter and a drummer, playing under a long blank white cloth banner hung between two poles.
fr_banderole_noun.note: Une banderole is a long banner carried in a march or hung up at a match.

fr_voter_verb.hook: "voh-TAY": MONSIEUR VERBE (red beret) VOTES, dropping his envelope into the clear ballot box while balancing a cup of TEA on its saucer in his other hand: VOTE-TEA
fr_voter_verb.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): Monsieur Verbe, a cheerful slim mime with white face paint, a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt, black suspenders, black trousers, white gloves and a red beret, little motion lines around his hands, standing at the table dropping a small blue envelope into a clear plastic ballot box with one hand, holding a teacup on a saucer in his other hand.
fr_voter_verb.note: Voter pour quelqu'un = to vote for someone. Une voix is a vote cast.

fr_partisan_noun.hook: "pahr-tee-ZAHN": a cheering SUPPORTER waves a giant wedge of PARMESAN cheese over his head like a foam finger: PARMESAN
fr_partisan_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a cheering young man with a blue-white-red rosette on his sweater waving a giant yellow wedge of parmesan cheese over his head.
fr_partisan_noun.note: Un partisan is a supporter of an idea or a person (un partisan du vélo). It is not party-political in the English sense of 'partisan'; in history it also means a resistance fighter.

fr_electeur_noun.hook: "ay-lehk-TUHR": an elderly VOTER in line gives A LECTURE to a bored teenager, wagging a finger, ballot envelope in hand: A-LECTURE
fr_electeur_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): an elderly woman voter with a white bun and a handbag wagging her finger and lecturing a bored teenage boy who rolls his eyes, both standing in line by the voting booths, she holds a small blue envelope.
fr_electeur_noun.note: Une électrice is a woman voter. La carte d'électeur is the voter card.

fr_elu_noun.hook: "ay-LEW": two friends lift LOU, the newly ELECTED official, onto their shoulders, and the crowd shouts 'HEY, LOU!': HEY-LOU
fr_elu_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/vote (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a beaming man in a suit lifted onto the shoulders of two laughing friends, waving both arms in victory.
fr_elu_noun.note: Un élu is any elected official (les élus municipaux); as an adjective, élu means elected or chosen.

fr_payant_adj.hook: "peh-YAHN": at the door a visitor PAYS for his ticket and the cashier gives an enormous YAWN: entry is PAYANT (not free): PAY-YAWN
fr_payant_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): at a small ticket table a man handing over a coin to a cashier lady who is yawning hugely with her hand near her mouth, a cash tin on the table.
fr_payant_adj.note: Payant means you have to pay (le parking est payant); the opposite is gratuit, free. Of a job or business: paying, profitable.

fr_rentable_adj.hook: "rahn-TAHBL": a beekeeper lady pays to RENT A TABLE at the fair and stacks it with honey jars that sell fast: PROFITABLE: RENT-A-TABLE
fr_rentable_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a beekeeper lady in a straw hat stacking golden honey jars on a trestle table, a man in an apron taking a coin from her for the table, a little pile of coins in a dish.
fr_rentable_adj.note: Rentable means profitable or worth it (un investissement rentable); it comes from la rente, income, not from English 'rent'.

fr_benevole_adj.hook: "bay-nay-VOL": BENNY, a VOLUNTEER in a green apron, keeps a beach ball going in a VOLLEY with the children, unpaid and happy: BENNY-VOLLEY
fr_benevole_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a cheerful young man in a green apron hitting a big striped beach ball up into the air in a volley, two small children reaching up for it.
fr_benevole_adj.note: Also a noun: un or une bénévole is a volunteer (unpaid helper).

fr_fierement_adv.hook: "fyeh-ruh-MAHN": a FIREMAN in his shiny helmet stands PROUDLY with his chest out and a new medal on his jacket: FIRE-MAN
fr_fierement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a firefighter in a dark blue uniform and a shiny silver helmet standing proudly with his chest out and hands on his hips, a round gold medal pinned on his jacket.
fr_fierement_adv.note: Fièrement comes from fier, proud (fier de son travail).

fr_paisiblement_adv.hook: "pay-zee-bluh-MAHN": an old man in a PAISLEY BLUE shirt dozes PEACEFULLY in a folding chair up on the stage: PAISLEY-BLUE-MAN
fr_paisiblement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): an old man with white hair in a blue paisley-patterned shirt dozing peacefully in a wooden folding chair up on the stage, his hands folded on his belly, eyes closed and a small smile.
fr_paisiblement_adv.note: Paisiblement comes from paisible, peaceful (from la paix, peace).

fr_carrement_adv.hook: "kah-ray-MAHN": a strongman CARRIES a whole upright piano across the hall in his arms: carrément, really, the WHOLE thing!: CARRY-MAN
fr_carrement_adv.why: English sound-alike painted in mairie/fetes (Oct 31 2026 MAIRIE1 build): a burly strongman with a curly mustache, in a sleeveless blue shirt, hugging a whole brown upright piano in his arms and carrying it across the hall, grinning.
fr_carrement_adv.note: Carrément is informal: 'totally, really' (c'est carrément génial) or 'bluntly, straight out' (il me l'a dit carrément).
